Alex: Heads-up — p95 spiked to ~320ms on hosted inference around 11:12 UTC. Autoscaler logs show scale-up started but GPUs weren't allocated for ~18s. Warm pool size reported 0 for a subset of shards. Not sure if kernel fallback + batch shrinkage amplified the latency. cc @Maya @Chris
infra-bot: [ALERT] latency_slo_violation count=42 service=runtime region=us-west-2 trace_id=8f3b2a2b
Maya: grabbing flamegraphs + perf traces now. Do we have a repro or a perf trace to attach?
Chris: saw something similar ~10:50 yesterday — kernel selection fell back to generic matmul because of a cuBLAS signature mismatch. Uploaded a profiler dump: s3://redwood-perf/1823456789/flame.svg
Priya: quick datapoint — batching histogram shows median batch size collapsed from 8 -> 2 at spike time (many short requests). Batching heuristic debounce appears to shorten window aggressively when QPS drops.
Alex: any correlation with KV cache hit rate? If miss rate spiked, KV population/loading + kernel warmup could add latency.
Sam: checked warm pool events: several hosts OOM-killed earlier due to model_kv growth. Eviction events at 11:04 and 11:07; warmpool auto-scaled down which left zero warm instances for some shards.
Maya: profiling shows ~12-16ms per-request overhead from kernel compile path being triggered on a new quantization profile. Log snippet: ```runtime: kernel_compiler: compiling kernel variant 'q4_0_sgemm' shape=(1024,128) took=0.012s```
Chris: that compile time + allocator stall matches the allocation delay. Autoscaler handoff logs show: `provisioner: handoff_timeout=15s` then `fallback: allocate_remote`. We should consider increasing handoff timeout to 30s to avoid premature fallback.
Priya: alternative mitigations: tweak batching debounce so when warmpool_size < 2 we use a slightly larger window. Quick sim patch: `batching.debounce_ms = if(warmpool_size < 2, 30, 10)` — reduces p95 in local sim by ~60ms for microbursts.
Alex: good set of leads. Action items: 1) bump provisioner handoff timeout to 30s (Chris) 2) apply debounce tweak to staging (Priya) 3) add `kernel_compile_count` metric and alert (Maya) 4) temporarily raise warmpool_min to avoid auto scale-down during churn (Sam).
Sam: will pin warm pool min size=2 for us-west-2 for the next 6 hours and monitor. Running: `kubectl get pods -l app=warmpool -o wide` to validate.
Maya: opened PERF-883 with traces + S3 link and sample logs. Adding @eng-sre and @eng-runtime for visibility. PR for compile metrics will land shortly.
Chris: rolling the provisioner timeout change to canary in us-west-2 now. Will keep an eye on `provisioner.handoff_duration` and latency.
Alex: thanks all — let's reconvene in 45m. :thumbsup:
